text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: elevated 5xx and 504 rate detected across gateway-prod clusters in us-west-2. Error rate spike started ~3432123300. Trigger: error_rate > 4% for 5m. Paging on-call.

Sam (on-call): acked. I'm on it. Starting quick blast radius check — which services show the most 5xx?

Priya SRE: I'm pulling dashboards. Looks like batch-scheduler queue depth is spiking on node-pool-batcher-3. Backend worker latency also rising. Gateway logs show timeout to scheduler: 'timeout waiting for batch' and 502s from gateway to runtime.

Marco (prod): customers reporting 504s for long-generation requests. Not seeing increased infra CPU or GPU usage; memory looks normal but scheduler queues are growing. Could be head-blocking batches.

Sam (on-call): copying logs now. Quick commands I'm running:
```
# tail recent gateway errors
kubectl logs -n prod gateway-prod -l app=gateway --since=10m | grep "timeout" | head -n 50

# check scheduler queue metrics
kubectl get --raw /apis/metrics/v1/namespaces/prod/services/scheduler | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, queueDepth: .queue.depth}'
```

Priya SRE: Found one hotspot: shard scheduler-3 is accepting many short requests with small tokens that block long requests due to batching policy. The batcher policy is grouping these into large head batches that stall heavy requests (head-blocking). Also noticed kv-cache churn for certain models, causing batcher to wait on KV lock.

Support Lead: Customer impact — several paying customers observed 5xx for inference calls between 12:15 and now. Support will surface top impacted customers and begin outreach. ETA for initial comms: 15m.

Sam (on-call): Mitigation plan:
1) Enable route-level fallback to lighter model for heavy routes.
2) Apply emergency rate-limit to low-priority tenant keys to shrink queue.
3) Restart batch-scheduler on node-pool-batcher-3 after pausing enqueue.
4) If restart fails, divert traffic to warm secondary scheduler-1.

Priya SRE: I'll run 2 and 3. Applying rate-limit to tenants matching label 'test-traffic' now.

Priya SRE: rate-limit applied:
```
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/rate_limit -d '{"selector":"label:test-traffic","rps":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```
Applied. Observability: queue depth dropped ~30% on shard-3 within 30s.

Sam (on-call): Pausing ingress to shard-3 for non-critical routes (cmd):
```
kubectl patch ingress gateway-prod -p '{"spec":{"rules":[{"host":"api.redwood-internal","http":{"paths":[{"backend":{"serviceName":"gateway-prod","servicePort":80}}, {"backend":{"serviceName":"gateway-prod","servicePort":80}}]}}]}}'
```
(yes, ugly quick patch, will revert)

Priya SRE: Restarting batch-scheduler process on node-pool-batcher-3 now. I'll do a controlled drain.

devops-bot: deploy-check: rolling-restart batch-scheduler node-pool-batcher-3 started by Priya SRE.

Priya SRE: Restart complete. Post-restart metrics look better. Queue depth returned to baseline for shard-3. Error rate dropped from 4.7% to 1.1% over 4m.

Marco (prod): Routing fallback engaged for long-halo requests; latency for these is temporarily higher but stable. We should watch for recurrence when traffic spikes.

Support Lead: Opening incident ticket for impacted customers and drafting initial status update. Notifying Account Execs for top 5 paying customers. Template note: impacted endpoints, start time, mitigation steps, next update in 30m.

Sam (on-call): Next actions — run longer soak for 20m, monitor batch-queue graphs, and prepare a postmortem stub. Priya, can you collect kernel thread dumps and scheduler logs for the window 12:10-12:30?

Priya SRE: Got them. Uploading artifacts to incident storage: s3://redwood-incidents/3432123456/

Priya SRE: hypothesis: small high-frequency requests caused head-blocking because batch-policy only prioritized by age not by estimated compute. Action item: adjust batching policy to include request-size heuristic and promote older long-running requests.

Sam (on-call): Agreed. Filing follow-up ticket for product + runtime to change batching heuristic and add per-tenant backpressure. Assigning to eng-runtime.

devops-bot: escalation: handing off to secondary on-call @Alex (on-call) for 1h to monitor.

Alex (sec on-call): ack. I'll keep watch. Please ping if any regression.

Support Lead: customer comms sent for major impacts; support queue updated with incident tag.

Sam (on-call): summary: root cause likely head-of-line blocking in batch-scheduler caused by many small/fast requests; led to queue buildup, gateway timeouts and 5xx. Immediate mitigations: rate-limited noisy tenants, paused non-critical routes, restarted batch-scheduler, enabled lighter model fallback. Monitoring shows error rate returning to normal but we will keep incident open until 2h stable.

Priya SRE: adding logs and timeline to incident ticket. Will draft RCA notes.

Sam (on-call): thanks team. If anything odd reappears, escalate immediately. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (monitoring): error rate back to normal, auto-clear in 30m if stable.
